hypothesis: The deployed GGUF has no output.weight, so llama.cpp's qwen35 loader creates the output head as a TENSOR_DUPLICATED copy of token_embd (Q8_0, 248,320 x 2,048) and KleidiAI repacks it into its CPU_KLEIDIAI buffer at load. The decider never reads it: decshim always loads with embeddings on and no pooling, and P1's prefill patch returns from the qwen35 graph before the LM head; the answer comes from the numpy pointer head over hidden states. Not creating that duplicate cuts cold model_load_mmap by about the time KleidiAI spends repacking it (about 1.7 s offline, E5) and peak memory by up to the size of the repacked copy, with bit-identical answers. Restore may also change if the snapshot shrinks; that is measured, not assumed.

changed_variable.name: whether llama.cpp creates (and so KleidiAI repacks) the unused tied output head at model load
changed_variable.baseline: ctl: LKAI_SKIP_TIED_OUTPUT unset. The patched loader takes upstream's path: output = create_tensor(token_embd, TENSOR_DUPLICATED), repacked into CPU_KLEIDIAI (P1's behaviour)
changed_variable.experiment: skip: LKAI_SKIP_TIED_OUTPUT=1. The duplicate is not created; model.output stays NULL. Same zip, same configuration, same weights object; nothing else differs

conclusion_template: Not creating the unused tied output head (LKAI_SKIP_TIED_OUTPUT=1) makes cold starts faster and every environment smaller, with every answer bit-identical. Mechanism, read from the loaded model in every environment (50 cold + 50 restore per arm): the head is skipped on all skip environments and none of ctl's, and the CPU_KLEIDIAI weight buffer is 1,998,856,192 -> 1,458,511,872 bytes (-540.3 MB, the repacked copy of token_embd). Deltas are skip minus ctl within one CPU part as read from /proc/cpuinfo (p50, 95% bootstrap CI, n ctl/skip). Host variability: three CPU parts appeared (0xd40, 0xd0c, 0xd4f, read in the function; no generation inferred), and every per-part CI and every (round, part) cell has the same sign for cold model_load_mmap, cold and restore first request, Restore Duration and Max Memory, so no rerun was needed; warm inference is null on both parts. Recommendation: adopt; it is one environment variable on a dormant loader patch, safe while the deployment never asks llama.cpp for logits (the patched LM head aborts rather than run without the head).
